title: Atari 2600: racing the beam — the kernel under a hard slice budget
summary: The Atari 2600 has no video frame buffer: the TIA paints whatever its registers say at the exact pixel the electron beam touches. Programmers feed registers in lockstep with the beam — 76 CPU cycles per scanline, 262 scanlines per NTSC frame (3 VSYNC + 37 VBLANK + 192 kernel + 30 overscan). All game logic lives in VBLANK/overscan; the visible kernel does nothing but feed the beam.
mechanism: Racing the beam: mid-scanline register writes (playfield/sprite/color) change the picture in lockstep with the electron gun; the horizontal blank (~22 cycles) is the only safe window for setup. Being one cycle late puts the wrong color in the wrong place, so cycle counts were hand-computed like drum beats.
decline: A cost-cut design that became a liability: framebuffer consoles (NES era) made beam-racing obsolete, and the 1983 crash + crude 2600 titles poisoned the well. The trick survived only in homebrew/demoscene.
revival_recipe: Frame-as-kernel execution: slice work into fixed-cost quanta with a hard per-slice budget and an inviolable reserved slice (the heartbeat) that always gets serviced — bounded time-slicing, not best-effort concurrency.
levi_application: Daemon supervision executor: an automation run sliced into bounded scanline-budget quanta so the heartbeat tick can never be starved by a runaway task. Same pattern for bounded simulation budgets.

title: Amiga Copper: timed choreography as a 3-instruction scored list
summary: The Copper is a display-synchronized co-processor running tiny programs of just three instruction types — MOVE (write a hardware register), WAIT (stall until the beam reaches x,y), SKIP (skip the next MOVE if a condition holds). Copper lists restart at each vertical blank, giving repeatable, zero-CPU, interrupt-free timed choreography: palette changes per scanline (copper/raster bars), split-screen modes, per-line scrolling.
mechanism: WAIT-until-position then MOVE: e.g. 'WAIT (0,64); MOVE COLOR00 $0f0; WAIT (0,128); MOVE COLOR00 $00f' draws two color zones with no CPU and no interrupts. A final WAIT for an impossible position parks the Copper until the next VBLANK restarts the list.
decline: Amiga's commercial death plus commodity GPUs absorbing the pattern (raster interrupts, shaders). The co-processor didn't lose technically — its platform died.
revival_recipe: Scored choreography: declarative lists of WAIT/EXEC/SKIP instructions executed by a tiny runner against a real or simulated clock, producing a receipt of what ran and when. No timers, no callbacks, no interrupt handlers — the list IS the program.
levi_application: Supervision recovery sequences and automation routines as Score lists: 'wait 5s for heartbeat; exec restart; wait until healthy (30s timeout); skip further if healthy'. Deterministic replay with a fake clock for tests and bounded simulation.

title: Palm Graffiti: narrow the input, gain reliability
summary: Palm's Newton competitors tried to recognize natural handwriting and failed; Palm shipped Graffiti — a constrained single-stroke shorthand alphabet users learn (A is an upside-down V without crossbar). Stroke end = character commit. Palm claimed near-100% accuracy once learned and >30 wpm. Most users competent in under 20 minutes.
mechanism: Constrain the input space instead of expanding the recognizer: one prescribed stroke per character in a dedicated input area, eliminating ambiguity at the source rather than resolving it with ML. Palm deliberately made the human adapt a little so the machine could be exact.
decline: Capacitive multitouch killed stylus PDAs; Graffiti survives as a third-party Android keyboard. The principle died with the platform, not on its merits.
revival_recipe: For high-stakes agent actions, define a closed set of unambiguous command forms (approve / deny / abort glyphs) instead of parsing free text; where reliability matters, narrow the channel rather than widening the model.
levi_application: LEVI consequential-action confirmations: a closed, exact-match command vocabulary (no fuzzy intent parsing) for approve/deny/abort — Plan-Preview-Permission already exists; Graffiti says make the permission vocabulary deliberately narrow and exact.

title: ZX Spectrum multicolor: exploit the hardware's re-read moment
summary: The Spectrum stored color separately from pixels: 256x192 bitmap plus a 32x24 attribute grid (one byte per 8x8 cell: ink, paper, bright, flash — borrowed from Teletext), costing £125 instead of true hi-res color. The infamous attribute clash was bypassed by demosceners who rewrote attribute RAM during the horizontal blank: the ULA re-reads attributes every scanline, so a new value per line yields 8x1 'multicolor/hicolour' — over 20 columns (CPU too slow for full width), or 8x2 over the full width (Nirvana+ engine).
mechanism: Change state in the sliver where the hardware re-samples: write the attribute row in horizontal blank, the ULA draws the next line with new colors. The impossible becomes possible by piggybacking the system's natural refresh boundary.
decline: A price-point compromise made into a feature by hackers; abandoned when better graphics hardware became cheap. Survives in demoscene folklore.
revival_recipe: Generalize: schedule state mutations at the system's natural re-read boundaries rather than adding new machinery. Refresh-synchronized mutation.
levi_application: Growth-loop bookkeeping: piggyback journal compaction and summary refresh on the heartbeat's natural boundaries instead of running a separate timer — same 'write in the blank' discipline. Bounded, predictable, zero new timers.
